name: r3a1-address-whole-object-no-silent-truncation
description: R3a-1 Outcome 1 whole-object read: a document longer than one response page must never be silently truncated. internal/address/address.go Read must flag a page that stops before the end with HasMore and a stable NextCursor, and may only set Complete when the page reaches the last byte. Weakening the cut-page guard `if end < total {` to a constant false makes every cut page report completion while data remains, so a client reassembling by pages would stop early. The existing evidence-backed tests kill that mutant: TestReadPageCutBeforeEndOffersNextCursor requires HasMore plus a cursor on a cut page, and TestReadReassemblesPagesToWholeOriginalHash requires the concatenation of all pages to equal the stored original.
baseline_meaning: On the unmutated tree Read reports HasMore and a non-empty NextCursor for a page cut before the end, sets Complete only on the final page, and the concatenation of all pages equals the stored original with a matching whole hash.
mutant_meaning: With the cut-page guard weakened to `if false` the branch that sets HasMore and NextCursor is never taken; every page, including one that stops before the end, reports Complete with no cursor. TestReadPageCutBeforeEndOffersNextCursor fails on the missing HasMore/cursor and TestReadReassemblesPagesToWholeOriginalHash stops after the first page and fails the reassembly/hash comparison (RED). The mutant is therefore killed by the registered probe, not vacuous.
runner: tests/contracts/mutation-runner/main.go executes this case from tests/contracts/mutation-registry.json under the GO_UNIT harness for the invariant entry `acceptance.r3a1.address.whole-object-no-silent-truncation`; the identical case is committed both here and in the registry so the proof is pinned to the product guard.
